content_note: Every rule here is intent-only: a name, an id and a logic line that names the detections the rule would join. There is no query, schedule, severity or alert mapping, so nothing in this file can be imported into a tenant as-is. Author the rule in the XSIAM console from the logic line.

rules.logic:
Operator-installed correlation rule (CortexSim never writes it to the tenant). Alert name EXACTLY as this rule's name; severity Medium (only Medium or higher opens or joins a case); Scheduled, every 10 minutes, query time frame 1 hour; alert field mapping: agent_hostname -> Host Name, agent_id -> Agent ID (the mapping CR-EDR-0023 uses); NO MITRE tag (the issue is matched by its name; a tagged issue would also be credited to the validation rows of every step that shares the technique, because a saved XQL and a correlation are one engine family to the matcher). UNTESTED: this XQL has not been run in any tenant. Its alter, comp, then filter shape follows CR-EDR-0023 on TTP-2026-0198, which that card records as tested read-only in the lab tenant on 2026-11-11. The ordering stage (the second alter, max() over a timestamp made by if(leg = ..., _time, null), and the two timestamp_diff conditions) is new here and has no tenant-tested precedent, and this rule is the scenario's only alert-backed row. BEFORE INSTALLING: run the XQL below once as an ordinary query in the tenant. If the tenant accepts it, install it as written. If the tenant rejects it, install the FALLBACK XQL printed after it instead. The fallback keeps the two legs, takes the comp and the final filter of CR-EDR-0023, and drops the ordering stage. It therefore has NO ORDER CHECK: it fires when both legs are present on one agent inside the time frame, in either order and any distance apart. It still fires on this chain. NO _time COLUMN, ON PURPOSE: neither query returns _time. The engine credits an alert to a run only if the alert is dated at or after the launch, and it dates an issue by detection_timestamp, then creation_time, then local_insert_ts, then _insert_time. A _time column in a rule's output could date the issue by an event instead of by the rule's own run, so none is returned. Which of those fields a correlation issue carries, and what they hold, has not been seen in this lab: the first lab run should record the timestamp fields of the CR-EDR-0027 issue. The rule is built only from process starts SIM-EDR-027 produces on one host: step-02 starts tar with an archive path under /var/tmp (the archived leg), and step-03 and step-04 start scp and ssh with a compressed-archive name on the command line (the carried leg). As written it fires when the latest SSH-client start is at or after the latest archiver start and no more than 900 seconds after it. It needs no connection, so it fires on an attempt as well as on a transfer, which is why this chain can raise it. It matches list and extract runs of an archiver as well as create runs. While the events stay inside the one-hour time frame it fires again on every scheduled run; alert suppression is the operator's choice. There is no current_time in the rule: the time frame bounds it. XQL:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| alter leg = if(action_process_image_name in ("tar", "zip", "7z", "7za") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^ ]*[.](tar[.]gz|tgz|tar[.]bz2|tbz2|tar[.]xz|txz|tar[.]zst|zip|7z)([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)", "archived", if(action_process_image_name in ("scp", "sftp", "ssh") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "[.](tar[.]gz|tgz|tar[.]bz2|tbz2|tar[.]xz|txz|tar[.]zst|zip|7z)([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)", "carried", "other"))
| filter leg in ("archived", "carried")
| alter archived_at = if(leg = "archived", _time, null), carried_at = if(leg = "carried", _time, null)
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events, max(archived_at) as last_archived, max(carried_at) as last_carried by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2 and timestamp_diff(last_carried, last_archived, "SECOND") >= 0 and timestamp_diff(last_carried, last_archived, "SECOND") <= 900
FALLBACK XQL (no order check; install it only if the tenant rejects the query above):
dataset = xdr_data
| filter agent_os_type = ENUM.AGENT_OS_LINUX
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| alter leg = if(action_process_image_name in ("tar", "zip", "7z", "7za") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "(/tmp/|/var/tmp/|/dev/shm/)[^ ]*[.](tar[.]gz|tgz|tar[.]bz2|tbz2|tar[.]xz|txz|tar[.]zst|zip|7z)([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)", "archived", if(action_process_image_name in ("scp", "sftp", "ssh") and action_process_image_command_line ~= "[.](tar[.]gz|tgz|tar[.]bz2|tbz2|tar[.]xz|txz|tar[.]zst|zip|7z)([^A-Za-z0-9]|$)", "carried", "other"))
| filter leg in ("archived", "carried")
| comp count_distinct(leg) as legs, count() as events, min(_time) as first_seen, max(_time) as last_seen by agent_hostname, agent_id
| filter legs >= 2
rules.name: EDR-027 Scratch Tarball Followed By SSH Carrier
